title: Buzzy as accompanist and the trio that inspired Hug
summary: Buzzy accompanied singers in the big clubs; Hug recalls a trio on radio with Oscar Marco and Bill Eastwood.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, man, yeah. Who did he accompany?
Who were some of the singers? Do you remember them?

You know, it's a funny thing. I'm ashamed to say this, but I know Buzzy so personally that it seems it's a shame to say that I can't remember his hometown. Buzzy came down here, oh, he's been to New Orleans, I guess maybe 40 years or better. And I can't remember exactly where he came from, and I can't remember some of the names that he worked with. He's worked with some real, but in fact, in recent years, he mentions some fellow by the name of Tommy Lynam. Lynam, huh?
Tommy Lynam, I think. Lynam, or Lynam?
Lynam, I think. Lynam, I think. Like a Lynam.

Lynam, Tommy Lynam. He's a very well-known entertainer, and Buzzy's worked with him as a, you know, as an accompanist. In fact, he wouldn't have anyone else Buzzy with him. But that's been in recent years now, I'd say in the past 10 years or so. Now, I don't know, I can't remember some of the names that he worked with before that. But he's accompanied pretty near every vocalist in the Wallens, and all the big clubs. He worked in all the big clubs like Club Forest and The Silver Slipper, and The Silver Slipper was really the place on Bourbon Street. He was always, he was always the top accompanist for any of those, any of those performers. I remember one trio that Buzzy worked with that was really a great inspiration to me. It was composed of him and Buzzy and Oscar Marco on violin, and Eastwood, Bill Eastwood on banjo. And I used to listen to them, the days when you had the old earphones, you know, and the crystal set. And they used to really play some fine jazz. They played a real rousing spirited type of thing that really, really moved, you know. You wouldn't call it ragtime or swing, but it was really a real good, they played real good fast stuff that really came off real well.
